set.body:
Goal
Turn the completed courts into an explicit product and scientific decision rather than preserving the phrase killer feature by assumption.

Decision rule
- Promote Transport v3 only if it passes invariants, adds order/partial-replay discrimination beyond fair baselines, is calibrated, and meets the runtime budget.
- If it is scientifically distinctive but tied on real item information, retain it as the symmetric explanatory alignment engine and keep Replay/density alternatives prominent.
- If it fails stability or runtime gates, keep the reference implementation experimental and record the no-go result.
- The independent Wang result remains confirmatory and may revise the role later; it cannot be used to tune the frozen model.

Acceptance criteria
- The public object exposes gaze_info_bits by default and nests matched coverage, spatial RMSE in declared units, local-order preservation, contraction, rank, and solver stability as diagnostics.
- Labels say optimized correspondence/alignment ambiguity, never posterior replay probability.
- autoplot provides registered overlay, gaze braid, raw-versus-registered paths, and a one-score evidence ledger with honest provenance.
- API supports one or multiple study episodes without silently changing normalization.
- Documentation explains Transport versus Replay and density, invariance contract, failure modes, calibration, candidate dependence, and bounded evidence.
- Synthetic/public fixtures reproduce examples; private Wynn data and outputs are absent from Git and package artifacts.
- Focused tests, full devtools tests, documentation generation, package build, and R CMD check pass with all new errors/warnings/notes resolved or explicitly bounded.
- A benchmark and decision report records score parity, runtime, scientific gates, claims permitted, claims prohibited, and the handoff to GW-10.
set.title: GW-18.11 Decide Transport's role and harden API, plots, docs, and release evidence
